plan.chapterName: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, chapter 1: Prerequisites
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain black line drawing of a right circular cylinder viewed in perspective from slightly above. The top face is rendered as a complete ellipse; the bottom is a partial ellipse whose far arc is omitted, and the two are joined by straight vertical lines at the left and right silhouette edges, so the solid reads as opaque. A horizontal arrow begins at the center of the top ellipse and points to the right until it touches the rim, with the italic label r sitting just above its shaft. Outside the body of the cylinder, to the right, a vertical double-headed arrow reaches from the level of the top rim down to the level of the bottom rim and is labeled h. There is no shading, no coordinate frame, and no numerical scale anywhere in the drawing. The two arrows isolate the only two measurements the solid requires, one running across the circular cross-section and one running along the axis. The picture accompanies the surface-area formula S = 2 pi r (r + h), fixing which distance the symbol r stands for and which the symbol h stands for.

elements: top circular cap rendered as a full ellipse (circle in the horizontal plane at y = +h/2)
bottom circular cap rendered as a partial ellipse with the far arc hidden (circle at y = -h/2)
lateral (side) surface of the right circular cylinder joining the two caps
left and right vertical silhouette edges where the lateral surface meets the viewing outline
horizontal radius arrow on the top cap from its center (0, h/2, 0) pointing +X to the rim (r, h/2, 0) with an arrowhead
italic label 'r' sitting just above the radius arrow shaft
vertical double-headed height arrow outside the body on the right at x ≈ r + 0.4 spanning y = -h/2 to y = +h/2
italic label 'h' to the right of the height arrow
NET VIEW: two outlined circles of radius r (the two caps) placed side by side
NET VIEW: one rectangle of width 2πr (circumference) and height h (the unrolled lateral surface)
NET VIEW: labels 'r' on a circle radius, 'h' on the rectangle height, and '2πr' along the rectangle width

interactions.label: radius r
interactions.teaches: Widening r enlarges both circular caps AND the circumference of the side, so r appears twice in S = 2πr(r + h); the radius arrow on the top face stretches with it

interactions.label: height h
interactions.teaches: Stretching h lengthens only the lateral surface while the caps stay the same size, isolating the 2πr·h side term from the 2πr² cap term

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Unrolling the cylinder into two circles plus a rectangle shows exactly where each piece of 2πr(r + h) = 2·(πr²) + (2πr)·h comes from: two cap areas and one side area

demo_steps.title: Default cylinder
demo_steps.narration: A right circular cylinder with radius r and height h. The horizontal arrow marks r across the top cap; the vertical double arrow marks h along the axis.

demo_steps.title: Grow the radius
demo_steps.narration: Increasing r to 1.8 widens the caps and the side together — r feeds both the cap area πr² and the circumference 2πr, which is why it appears twice in the formula.

demo_steps.title: Grow the height
demo_steps.narration: Increasing h to 2.6 stretches only the lateral wall; the caps are unchanged, so h contributes solely through the 2πr·h side term.

demo_steps.title: Unroll to the net
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the net lays the surface flat: two circles of area πr² (the caps) and a rectangle of width 2πr by height h (the side). Adding them gives S = 2πr(r + h).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: cylinder axis vertical along +Y, centered at origin; radius r ∈ [0.5,2] (default 1), height h ∈ [0.5,3] (default 1.5), so the body spans y ∈ [-h/2, +h/2] and x,z ∈ [-r, r]. Top cap circle at y=+h/2, bottom cap at y=-h/2. Radius arrow: line from (0, h/2, 0) to (r, h/2, 0) with a small cone arrowhead at the rim; label 'r' at ~(r/2, h/2+0.18, 0). Height arrow: vertical double-headed line at x = r + 0.45 from y=-h/2 to y=+h/2; label 'h' at (r+0.7, 0, 0). Palette: line/edge black #000000, cylinder lateral fill very light grey #f2f2f2 at ~0.85 opacity, cap fill white #ffffff, background white. NET layout (camera-facing plane at z=0): left circle center (-r-1.2, 0.6, 0) radius r; right circle center (r+1.2, 0.6, 0) radius r; rectangle centered at (0, -h/2-0.4, 0) with width 2πr and height h. Net labels: 'r' on a horizontal radius of the left circle, 'h' on the rectangle's right edge, '2πr' centered under the rectangle's bottom edge. Surface-area formula S = 2πr(r+h) = 2πr² + 2πrh.
interactionPlan.notes: Three.js: build the solid as an open-ended CylinderGeometry(r, r, h, 64) for the lateral wall plus two CircleGeometry(r, 64) caps rotated to horizontal, each with a black EdgesGeometry/LineLoop outline so the silhouette reads like the line drawing; hide the bottom cap's far half by relying on depth (opaque caps) rather than trimming. Rebuild or scale geometry on every slider input (set cylinder.scale or regenerate BufferGeometry) and reposition the r and h arrows/labels to track r and h. For the Net toggle, keep a separate Group of two ring/line circles and a plane rectangle (width = 2*Math.PI*r, height = h) and show/hide the two groups; recompute the rectangle width whenever r changes so the circumference visibly grows. Use a Sprite or canvas-texture plane for the italic r, h, and 2πr labels so they always face the camera. Keep OrbitControls enabled but constrained so the learner can confirm the roundness of the caps.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radius r: the learner drags the top-face radius arrow and the cylinder widens while the circular caps and lateral wrap update, making clear that r affects both cap area and circumference in S = 2 pi r(r + h).
- Slider for height h: the learner drags the vertical height arrow and the cylinder stretches upward without changing cap size, making clear that h changes only the lateral surface area contribution.
- Toggle between solid cylinder and surface-area net: the learner switches from the 3D view to two circles plus a rectangle, making clear how the measured r and h generate the formula's cap and side terms.

authoredContext:
A right circular cylinder with radius r and height h has the surface area S (in square units) given by the formula S=2πr(r+h). See the figure. Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius 6 in. and height 9 in. Leave the answer in terms of π.

Right circular cylinder

A right circular cylinder with an arrow extending from the center of the top circle outward to the edge, labeled: r. Another arrow beside the image going from top to bottom, labeled: h.
